summary: Angular holdout ran RED under the frozen adapter. Freeze fingerprint intact before and after; zero frozen-subtree and zero app-source hand edits. The engine composed a changeset for pigallery2 without crashing (214 scanned / 3 application files changed, 3 workspace, tslint.json removed, 6 unhandled, 8 declared differences) and applied it to .versionless/work/angular-pigallery2/target/app. The migrated closure does not install (ETARGET + ERESOLVE), so no target build and no two-run byte comparison exists; none is claimed. Seven gaps itemised by package, file, line and quoted diagnostic — 3 install, 4 compile — including a family-prefix overreach and two capabilities the adapter exports but never calls. tsc, lint, freeze check and the new 12-test suite pass.
open_questions: RED, install stage: the migrated closure is refused by npm 8. G1 @angular-devkit/build-optimizer ETARGET — the cell's `@angular-devkit/` family-prefix rule writes ^16.2.0 for a package that stops at 0.1302.1 (deprecated, folded into build-angular); no 16.x was ever published. G2 ng2-slim-loading-bar@4.0.0 ERESOLVE on peer @angular/core '^2.4.7 || ^4.0.0'; 4.0.0 is the latest dist-tag, so the reading is no-successor. G3 ngx-toastr@10.0.4 ERESOLVE on peer @angular/common '>=6.0.0 <9.0.0' and independently on rxjs ^6.1.0; lines 17.0.0-19.1.0 declare '>=16.0.0-0' and would satisfy this cell. None of the three is in ANGULAR_16_ECOSYSTEM_PACKAGES, and no prior Angular vertical declares any of them.

RED, compile stage (measured in a separate probe tree, never the lane). G4: ngx-bootstrap@5.1.0, @yaga/leaflet-ng2@1.0.0 and jw-bootstrap-switch-ng2@2.0.5 declare open-ended @angular peers ('>=7.0.0', '>=2.0.0'), so they resolve silently and then fail inside their own published declarations — 7 of 8 TS2314 are in ngx-bootstrap's `static forRoot(): ModuleWithProviders`, plus TS2416 in leaflet-ng2's geojson.directive.d.ts. An open-ended peer is not evidence of compatibility. G6: frontend/app/app.module.ts:122 writes a webpack inline loader chain, require(`raw-loader!../translate/messages.${locale}.xlf`); raw-loader@1.0.0 was an undeclared transitive of devkit 0.801.2 and devkit 16.2 does not ship it. G7: overlay.service.ts:27 msOverflowStyle left lib.dom.d.ts between TS 3.4.5 and 5.1.3.

SHARPEST FINDING (G5), and the one that is a wiring defect rather than a knowledge gap: packages/frameworks/angular/src/module-with-providers-type-argument.ts and unparameterised-base-class.ts are exported from the package index and imported by NOTHING inside the package. migrateAngularCliEraWorkspace imports thirteen capability modules and neither is among them, so the composed changeset can never run them for any application. They would answer frontend/app/app.routing.ts:71 (TS2314 ModuleWithProviders) and frontend/app/ui/settings/_abstract/abstract.settings.component.ts:14 (NG2007 undecorated base class) exactly. This is the same defect the super-productivity lane recorded against entry-components-removal — which has since been composed in — recurring on two more capabilities. 26 of the 28 modules the index exports are never imported by the era migration; whether the other 24 are reachable by another path was not audited by this unit.

Scope note for the next unit: the target build x2 the packet asked for does not exist and cannot until at least G1-G3 are answered, because a build needs an installed closure. Answering them is a frozen-adapter edit and was therefore out of scope here. Also unanswered: the era production build is an i18n build driven by the repository's gulp task with four ViewEngine i18n flags the 16.2 CLI no longer accepts, and angular.json declares no i18n for the workspace migration to read — so even a green migrated build would not be output-comparable to the baseline. The adapter's template-i18n-runtime capability is among the exported-but-never-imported set.
